note: The sins this project has reported to code-commandments. A judge reads a sin listed here as reported rather than active, so deleting this file makes every one of them active again and invites a second report of each. The flagged line is kept as a hash, never as text: this file is committed and the issues it names are public.

14a8881cc052ee975b88febe24fe3b2a71c43a03.reason: The developer request inspector preserves arbitrary JSON bodies and header names exactly for display. These values have no fixed record keys and are never interpreted as domain records; the headers are a dynamic mapping and the body is opaque JSON.

2254f2c20725ec002a1f4f54a33696208c18d841.reason: BackgroundCommands.alias_names applies configured alias policy to parsed shell commands. Journal-part selection now belongs to ShellLine.parts_running_journal_command; this method calls that API and checks names through the injected ShellAliases interface, then preserves the hook-provided alias names. It does not select programs by traversing shell.parts. ShellLine cannot decide which command names are configured aliases. The remaining traversal is the policy-over-flat-fields exception documented by the tell-dont-ask skill.

9260d68892dd2ba1a0ae25e66d4b060851ebd589.reason: Task.closed_at is a genuine nullable: None for every open task, set by close() and cancel() through moved(closed_at=timestamp) at task.py:46 and 49, reset to None by reopen() through moved(closed_at=None) at task.py:55. Task is a frozen dataclass and moved() is its only writer, so the reset is a keyword argument of a call. The only Python read of a Task's closed_at is task_group.py:16, which places it in a dict without dereferencing it. Pin, dump and agent block models carry a closed_at of the same name with guards.
